data.hypothesis: The previous valid OpenMP candidate used a serial cutoff of 512 options per requested worker. Lowering the cutoff to 256 options per effective worker, while limiting the requested team to min(threads, n), tests whether parallelizing medium workloads pays off without creating idle workers or exceeding the passed CPU budget. The controller must measure the cutoff's overhead and any gain; no result is assumed here.

memory_lessons.applicability: Useful evidence that the outer loop can be parallelized while preserving varied-input correctness; it does not identify an optimal small-work cutoff or establish speedup for this candidate.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior OpenMP candidate was valid on eight varied correctness cases and measured 1.430 ms mean versus the serial baseline's 7.529 ms mean under this campaign. That observation alone does not isolate the cause of the difference or establish a cutoff optimum.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this lower per-worker cutoff, especially cases near the serial/parallel boundary and available thread counts, and compare overhead with the prior candidate.

data.notes: This candidate retains a serial path and assigns each parallel iteration one distinct result index. The prior measured OpenMP variant and baseline are controller observations; this candidate has not been measured. The proposed cutoff is based on per-worker work, not a particular published n.
transformations: Factored the per-option formula into an inline helper used by both serial and parallel paths.
Added a static-scheduled OpenMP loop with num_threads(min(threads, n)) so the requested team does not exceed the supplied budget or the number of iterations.
Used a per-effective-worker cutoff of 256 options to retain the serial path for small workloads and contrast the prior candidate's larger work-grain assumption.
